mechanism_narrative: The sustained high level of residential mobility (above 20% baseline) and consistently low levels across all other categories indicate a persistent preference for staying home, which will continue to suppress retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated above 20%.

mechanism_narrative: A slight increase in WORKPLACES mobility from its current low point, signaling a return to offices, will lead to a modest rebound in retail and recreation activity as people combine work with leisure over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days even if WORKPLACES rises by more than 2 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of declining PARKS mobility due to colder winter weather and persistently low TRANSIT usage, reflecting ongoing public health concerns, will jointly depress retail and recreation activity further over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days, despite PARKS and TRANSIT remaining low or declining.

mechanism_narrative: Following the post-holiday lull and associated mobility dips observed in RETAIL_REC, a natural behavioral rebound in non-essential outings will drive a slight increase in retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks, assuming no new severe restrictions.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or remains flat over the next 28 days, without new severe restrictions being implemented.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility continues its recent downward trend and falls below -35% from baseline, it signals a broader deterioration in public confidence and willingness to leave home, which will further reduce RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days, even if GROCERY_PHARM falls below -35%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility and an increase in WORKPLACES mobility indicates a shift away from home-based activities, which will free up time and inclination for retail and recreation, leading to a modest rise over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by >1 point AND WORKPLACES rises by >1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, despite a concurrent decrease in RESIDENTIAL and increase in WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: The consistently low levels of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility over the past four weeks indicate that a significant portion of the population is not commuting or engaging in out-of-home work, directly limiting opportunities for associated retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remaining at current low levels.

mechanism_narrative: If local authorities signal an upcoming easing of restrictions, even a small uptick in PARKS mobility could precede a broader increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks, as people anticipate more freedom and plan outings.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, even if PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week and policy easing is signaled.
